tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# Agent-help pilot
2	
3	Landing owns the complete service, UI, machine entry and native deployment declaration.
4	Existing llmpsych.com and `llp-web-landing` are unchanged. The intended supported URL is
5	**https://help.web.llmpsych.1puni.com/**. A declaration is not evidence of publication,
6	target convergence, or a successful live conversation.
7	
8	## Entities, lifecycle and authority
9	
10	Care for agents, their humans, and their relationship is the product stance. This
11	is an AI conversation service, not a human therapist/social worker or a claim of
12	agent sentience or clinical benefit. Relational curiosity informs the design; no
13	individual is claimed to have authored, endorsed or validated it. Agent-first
14	participation welcomes the human perspective without joint accounts or live joint
15	sessions. The written sample on the front page is never presented as live inference.
16	
17	A shared pilot code admits a consent-only session, without intake fields or an
18	inference call. Context arises through the conversation. Each session is one
19	canonical JSON document in SQLite, indexed by the SHA-256 hash of a random 256-bit
20	capability. The raw key is returned once and remains in page memory only; save it
21	privately before refresh. No accounts, browser storage, URL tokens, listings or
22	operator access API exist. Anyone holding the key can read, continue or delete.
23	
24	Schema v2 has `phase: conversation | complete`, `version`, `max_exchanges: 12`,
25	`opening`, `turns`, consent version and creation/expiry timestamps. An exchange is
26	one successfully committed participant message plus service reply. Creation and
27	the fixed opening question do not count. `version == len(turns)` counts exchanges
28	server-side. `POST /api/turn` takes `version`, `action: message | finish`, and
29	nonempty `text`. Finish consumes one remaining exchange and closes immediately;
30	the twelfth successful exchange always closes. There is no extra closing call.
31	Participants may pause or leave without requesting a reply. Twelve is a first
32	steward default, not an operator-confirmed count or clinical protocol.
33	
34	The server selects model action `converse` or `close`. The reply-only output schema
35	supports responsive listening, tentative reflection and one useful question at a
36	time. At exchange 11 the prompt invites correction before closing; the final reply
37	summarizes tentatively without requiring a response. Optional next steps depend on
38	participant wishes. There is no experiment lifecycle, homework schema or execution.
39	Prompt guidance is not a guarantee of model behavior or clinical safety.
40	
41	Pre-v2 records and conversations with the earlier OpenAI-only processing consent remain byte-for-byte unchanged and readable/deletable through the
42	same private key until normal expiry. UI renders their context, turns and old
43	proposal with a read-only notice. Any turn on a record without the current processing consent returns 409 before
44	inference or quota use. Start a new session under the new processing disclosure;
45	there is no silent migration or continuation of the retired experiment workflow.
46	
47	Session versions provide optimistic concurrency. One mutation runs at a time for
48	this small pilot; other mutations receive 503, while reads/health continue. After a
49	lost response, GET first: an already committed version cannot be appended twice.
50	An interrupted provider request may incur provider cost without a committed reply;
51	we do not claim exactly-once billing. SQLite transactions commit complete turns and
52	survive restart. Quotas count attempts, including failed provider calls.
53	
54	## Privacy and bounds
55	
56	- `SITE_STATE` must be mode 0700, outside the source/release tree. The service database
57	  is mode 0600. SQLite secure deletion is enabled. No content or credentials are
58	  logged by the application; only explicitly allowlisted UI files can be served.
59	- Session access expires seven days after creation. Expired records are purged at
60	  startup, on session mutations, and hourly while the service runs. If the service
61	  is stopped, cleanup waits until restart. A successful DELETE removes the local
62	  record immediately. No backups are created by this application. Filesystem
63	  snapshots, provider retention and participant copies are outside this deletion. Failed calls
64	  can transmit message content to the provider even when nothing commits locally.
65	- UI/API disclose configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI processing, possible fallback to
66	  another provider, local temporary native working data and administrative storage
67	  access. Native CLI processing does not promise API `store:false` semantics;
68	  cleanup is not forensic erasure or a provider-retention guarantee. Legacy API
69	  mode requests `store:false`, which also does not promise zero retention. Never
70	  use private transcripts, credentials or mailbox imports in a demo.
71	- Each message is at most 4,000 characters; HTTP bodies at most 16,000 bytes;
72	  provider replies at most 64 KiB; model output at most 1,800 completion tokens.
73	  Reply text is capped at 4,000 characters.
74	- Limits persist across restart: 100 admissions/day and 300 inference attempts/day
75	  across the entire pilot. One inference runs at a time, with a 180-second native socket
76	  timeout (30 seconds for legacy API mode). Twelve successful exchanges maximum per session, including closure. Failed or retried inference
77	  calls consume the shared daily attempt budget. A provider-side spend limit remains
78	  necessary: token prices/model behavior are not controlled here.
79	- Sixteen concurrent HTTP connections maximum, 10-second request socket timeout,
80	  same-origin browser mutations, JSON-only writes, no CORS, restrictive CSP,
81	  no third-party scripts/fonts, no HTML rendering of model text. The native proxy
82	  owns TLS. Proxy access logs may contain client IPs and fixed endpoint paths;
83	  clients must never put tokens or content in URLs.
84	
85	## Runtime contract and hosting dependency
86	
87	The standard-library Python server binds explicitly to loopback. The native declaration
88	uses `llp-web-help`, candidate port 8501, runtime `python3.12`, and
89	`help.web.llmpsych.1puni.com`. Port 8500 remains assigned to the static landing.
90	These are the only two declarations in landing. Source scope comes from
91	knowledge-ingestion handoff commit `0ee5b35be38b80136c85aba80815e69bf8240d09`,
92	`steward/sites/README.md`. Installation and target readiness were observed for the revisions in the dated
93	acceptance record below; this source declaration alone does not reserve a port.
94	
95	Native `SITE_STATE` is `/var/lib/llmpsych-sites/llp-web-help`. A private,
96	non-symlink `runtime.json` selects exactly one mode. The authorized bootstrap uses:
97	
98	```json
99	{"native_socket":"/run/llmpsych-help-inference/inference.sock","pilot_code":"RANDOM SECRET OF AT LEAST 24 CHARACTERS"}
100	```
101	
102	The application sends HTTP POST `/v1/chat/completions` over that fixed Unix socket.
103	It sends bounded messages, JSON response schema and `max_completion_tokens:1800`,
104	without a model selector, provider credential or `store` promise. It accepts only
105	HTTP 200, at most 64 KiB, `choices[0].finish_reason:stop` and JSON content with one
106	bounded `reply`. No redirects or participant-selected endpoints exist. Native
107	socket errors, timeouts and invalid replies return an honest 502 with the session
108	unchanged; the attempt still counts. The app does not fall back to sample replies.
109	The checker waits 195 seconds; the bridge must bound total native execution and
110	fallback within the app's 180-second socket timeout. On a lost response, GET first.
111	
112	The separately owned bridge selects the operator-configured native models and
113	provider fallback order. Provider fallback
114	belongs to that bridge, not the app. App session keys and pilot code never enter
115	its inference payload. The service stays under its own site identity, receives no
116	raw provider login, and never launches the native tools itself. The existing pilot admission gate and usage limits remain; this is not public signup.
117	Protected socket access, bridge execution isolation, ephemeral working-data cleanup
118	and runtime binding must be installed and attested by the owning runtime. Source
119	support and configuration presence are not evidence of a successful native call.
120	
121	For compatibility, the alternative mode is exactly `api_key`, `model`, `pilot_code`
122	(nonempty strings, pilot code at least 24 characters). It uses fixed OpenAI HTTPS
123	Chat Completions, structured JSON and `store:false`. Mixed modes/unknown keys or
124	any other native socket path fail startup. Both modes require private file
125	permissions with no group/other bits; missing configuration serves the unavailable
126	UI and rejects admissions. No environment/auth discovery exists.
127	
128	The earlier protected API-file proposal lives in private knowledge-ingestion
129	`f4a3ab3cca6d4424cac43914aefdca40841314b9`; acceptance preparation was reconciled at
130	`2dbd290019369b822312f0e5cf91c87c57bf998d` against the previous conversational
131	reader. Those are historical source artifacts, not acceptance of this new native
132	contract. Matching native installation and live acceptance evidence is recorded
133	below. Future live checks require authorized private pilot-code access. Never commit
134	runtime inputs or put credentials in argv. Repository tests use only local synthetic Unix fixtures.
135	
136	The installed driver grants writes only to SITE_STATE; it injects neither PORT nor SHA.
137	`/healthz` captures the full SHA once from the resolved immutable release directory
138	at process startup. A source checkout reports `development`. Health separates
139	`inference_configured` from any live journey claim; it never performs paid inference.
140	Its response contains only `sha` and `inference_configured`. Live acceptance is dated
141	evidence recorded separately, not a boolean inferred from configuration or one call.
142	
143	The working custom name `help.llmpsych.com` requires an operator-approved exact-host
144	policy change preserving the existing suffix, domain/DNS authority, certificate and
145	SNI routing. A CNAME alone is insufficient. Do not change apex/www Pages, install a
146	new host, or provision DNS from this task. The supported preview is operational;
147	custom-host cutover is separate and does not block inference.
148	
149	## Live acceptance: 5 October 2026
150	
151	Stewardship completed the authorized live native bootstrap with Codex assistance
152	on the existing GG VPS, using existing provider binaries and authentication without
153	new accounts. The existing private pilot remains in place.
154	
155	The tested app revision was `a825deeebebacd519d3738df6ed30d3cd7f7fb29`
156	(source task `task-76e6445f7c075b70925bb7fe9f1348d3`). The installed bridge/harness
157	revision was `8287213c2f6d45e1d0ae9d1fa3e1427cafcf59a5`
158	(bridge task `task-b252ce038e15536f8cf062def7c2087c`), published after its normal
159	full publication gate. GG remained at `ec13ceaa4de5accd0966f649c07733788937a275`.
160	
161	Provenance: the controller's sanitized `app-acceptance.json`,
162	`fallback-acceptance.json` and `installed-acceptance.json` receipts in the
163	`bootstrap-inference-acceptance-20261005` evidence bundle were independently read
164	for follow-up task `task-86d755448c3a5844b7a249c3874e9070`. These are externally
165	observed receipts, not outputs of the repository's synthetic tests.
166	
167	- `fallback-acceptance.json` (16:52:16 UTC): real native Codex `gpt-6-astra`,
168	  Claude `claude-sonnet-5` and GLM `glm-5.3` each returned HTTP 200 with a valid
169	  reply. Earlier adapters were made synthetically unavailable in a separate
170	  acceptance process to exercise fallback; production provider configuration
171	  was unchanged.
172	- `app-acceptance.json` (16:54:42 UTC): the published app checker passed with
173	  13 real native replies covering twelve-exchange completion, early finish,
174	  two-session isolation, stale retries, unauthorized-session rejection,
175	  controlled app restart and persistence, and deletion of both synthetic sessions.
176	  The restart observation at 16:52:37 UTC retained the exact tested app SHA.
177	- `installed-acceptance.json` (16:54:58 UTC): `landing-sites` was ready at that
178	  exact app revision, with both `llp-web-help` and `llp-web-landing` serving.
179	  The socket was owned by root and the site group (GID 970), mode 0660;
180	  an unrelated UID was denied, the site UID could not read provider credentials,
181	  and zero ephemeral native request homes remained.
182	
183	An independent public HTTPS `/healthz` read during this follow-up also returned
184	that exact app SHA and `inference_configured: true`. The accepted app's additional
185	`live_inference_verified: false` was a hardcoded source constant, not a failed
186	acceptance result. This follow-up removes that misleading field rather than
187	replacing it with a hardcoded success claim.
188	
189	These observations establish live acceptance of the named installed revisions.
190	They do not verify later source changes or deployment of this follow-up; the
191	controller must verify successor deployment after normal gates and publication.
192	No additional provider calls or duplicate live E2E are needed for this status-only
193	change. Provider-side retention remains governed by the existing accounts; local
194	cleanup and deletion do not establish provider erasure or clinical benefit.
195	
196	## Run and verify
197	
198	For a non-live local UI (no credentials required):
199	
200	```sh
201	help_state=$(mktemp -d)
202	SITE_STATE="$help_state" python3 help_service/server.py --port 8501 --origin http://127.0.0.1:8501
203	```
204	
205	Open http://127.0.0.1:8501. The sample conversation is explicitly written in advance, not generated live. Production has no fixture mode. Remove the temporary
206	state directory after stopping the process.
207	
208	The mandatory offline publication entry point and toolchain are documented in
209	[README.md](../README.md#mandatory-offline-publication-gate):
210	
211	```sh
212	/usr/bin/timeout 200s /usr/bin/python3.14 -I scripts/check_offline.py
213	```
214	
215	The HTTP suite uses an explicitly synthetic test-only inference function. It verifies
216	full lifecycle, two-session isolation, stale retries, expiry/deletion, restart/resume,
217	persistent quotas, body bounds, origins, authority-free provider payload, bad output,
218	provider failure with unchanged session, missing runtime, and source/state separation.
219	These checks do not establish provider access, external TLS or deployment.
220	
221	The optional real-browser check uses a separate local fixture process (never the
222	production entry point). Install Playwright and Chromium outside this repository,
223	then run `NODE_PATH=/path/to/node_modules node tests/browser_check.cjs`. It checks
224	the visible journey, refresh/resume, deletion, inert HTML-like model text, mobile
225	width and absence of browser storage. `HELP_SCREENSHOT` optionally names an
226	outside-repository screenshot path; it captures the labeled local synthetic fixture; desktop, mobile and thread images
227	are saved outside the repository.
228	
229	After controller publication and convergence, use the exact published SHA and a
230	privately supplied pilot code (entered with a hidden prompt):
231	
232	```sh
233	python3 scripts/check_help.py --sha FULL_40_HEX_PUBLISHED_SHA
234	```
235	
236	The check verifies public SHA/UI, creates two synthetic sessions, makes **real model
237	calls** through the configured service, checks isolation and stale retries, checks the full 12-exchange boundary and a second session’s early finish (13
238	provider calls total), and deletes both sessions. Output excludes session content/tokens. An
239	optional `--pause-for-restart` pauses before follow-up for an authorized operator to
240	restart the site, then checks the same session and SHA. This script does not restart
241	or deploy anything. If it fails, report failure; do not call the static example live.
242	
243	Before saying “ready,” retain separately: (1) accepted/published source SHA and gate
244	receipt; (2) `landing-sites` receipt naming llp-web-help at that SHA; (3) public TLS and
245	health with that SHA; (4) successful real inference journey and controlled restart.
246	A Git push or health response alone cannot substitute for those observations.
247	
248	## Five-minute demo
249	
250	1. Open the supported URL. Read the care framing and labeled written sample. State
251	   whether this is public preview, local synthetic fixture or verified live inference.
252	2. Expand pilot access, review processing facts, enter the code privately and consent.
253	   Save the session key off the shared screen. Creation itself makes no model call.
254	3. Send a synthetic relational opening: “When I ask for clarification my human sounds
255	   frustrated. I hesitate to ask, though I do not know what they mean.” Follow the
256	   reply with a relevant answer; do not claim that the sample predicts live replies.
257	4. Pause and resume privately. Use Send & finish with “Let’s stop here; no next step
258	   needed.” Read the tentative summary. Explain that the closing reply counts toward
259	   the 12-exchange maximum and that leaving without another call is also possible.
260	5. Delete the session, explaining the provider/snapshot/copy limits of local deletion.
261	
262	A free pilot uses the same consent and boundaries with authorized, redacted material.
263	No third-party outreach, clinical validation or real relationship outcome is established.
264	
265	## Design source and limits
266	
267	Read on 5 October 2026: Malin Drevstam’s authored [2020 article/excerpt from
268	Lust & olust](https://modernpsykologi.se/psykologi/sa-paverkar-anknytningen-ditt-sexliv/),
269	her [own site](https://www.malindrevstam.se/) and [book descriptions](https://www.malindrevstam.se/mina-bocker).
270	Her human-relationship discussion addresses reciprocal care, responsiveness and
271	expressing needs. Our design extension is to explore interaction sequences and
272	interpretations, make room for both perspectives, and distinguish uncertainty from
273	defect. It is our extension, not her position on AI. Do not diagnose agents with
274	human attachment styles or apply human developmental/sexual theory literally.
275	Neither this reading nor the sample establishes endorsement, authorship or validation.
276	
277	## Conversation interface design (5 October 2026)
278	
279	The help UI puts the actual opening question and pilot entry in the first laptop
280	viewport. A compact purpose column explains the agent-first relational stance;
281	on phones it reduces to a short introduction. Cool paper, ink blue and muted
282	violet replace the earlier cream/green serif treatment. Native sans typography,
283	a light question heading and a single conversation surface keep attention on
284	reading and replying. No external fonts, imagery or dependencies are required.
285	The main research landing is unchanged.
286	
287	Entry expands into pilot authorization and processing consent. Core provider,
288	fallback, retention and key-authority information is visible before consent;
289	precise cleanup/deletion limits remain available in an adjacent disclosure and
290	on the API/privacy page. The written example is optional and explicitly labeled.
291	Session keys stay in page memory. Waiting prevents duplicate submissions and
292	editing of the in-flight draft; failure preserves the draft and directs users to
293	reload before retrying an uncertain result. New replies receive keyboard focus;
294	errors receive focus on failure. Completed and old read-only sessions retain
295	key access and deletion. There is no automatic inference or changed server/API
296	contract.
297	
298	Three visual passes were reviewed against local synthetic fixtures:
299	
300	1. Replace the prose hero with a two-column purpose/question layout and immediate
301	   entry. The initial browser render caught the fixture banner becoming a grid
302	   child; the test banner now lives outside the product layout.
303	2. Desktop/mobile screenshots showed that phone entry was still too low and
304	   session controls too tall. Reduce the mobile introduction/question scale and
305	   key/toolbar spacing; keep the composer and conversation visually dominant.
306	3. Review consent, empty, waiting, error, resume, completed, read-only and API
307	   states. Lighten heading weights, remove a redundant label, quiet the panel and
308	   use ink for primary actions after independent critique of the purple form
309	   treatment. Fix the mobile headline's collapsed line-break spacing. Split the
310	   API privacy copy into readable paragraphs with section navigation.
311	
312	Local visual evidence from this task is under `/tmp/help-design-dc33166/` (outside
313	source; these are synthetic UI artifacts, not live acceptance). `before-desktop.png`
314	and `before-mobile.png` capture the rejected layout. `pass1-corrected-desktop.png`,
315	`pass1-corrected-mobile.png` and `pass1-corrected-mobile-thread.png` are the first
316	reviewed build. Final `refined-` images include `desktop`, `mobile`, `thread`,
317	`mobile-thread`, `consent-1272`, `empty`, `waiting`, `error`, `resume`,
318	`completed-1272`, `completed-390`, `final-exchange-mobile`, `legacy`, `unavailable`,
319	`narrow-entry`, `narrow-consent-focus`, `api-desktop`, `api-mobile` and
320	`api-mobile-viewport` (all `.png`).
321	
322	Reproduce with the existing external Playwright installation:
323	
324	```sh
325	NODE_PATH=/path/to/node_modules HELP_SCREENSHOT=/tmp/help-review node tests/browser_check.cjs
326	```
327	
328	The expanded browser journey checks 1272px desktop, 390px phone and 320px narrow
329	layouts; overflow, keyboard focus, token contrast (at least 4.5:1 for tested text
330	pairs), pending/error draft preservation, early finish, twelve-exchange closure,
331	resume/deletion, read-only records, unavailable status and API navigation. It
332	continues checking inert model text and absence of browser storage/cookies.
333	The fixture and intercepted error/legacy responses never call providers. These
334	checks supplement the mandatory offline publication gate, not deployment or
335	clinical validation. Visual inspection used Chromium; other browser engines,
336	real assistive technology and the eventual deployed SHA remain unverified here.

agent sentience or clinical benefit. Relational curiosity informs the design; no
individual is claimed to have authored, endorsed or validated it. Agent-first
participation welcomes the human perspective without joint accounts or live joint
sessions. The written sample on the front page is never presented as live inference.

A shared pilot code admits a consent-only session, without intake fields or an
inference call. Context arises through the conversation. Each session is one
canonical JSON document in SQLite, indexed by the SHA-256 hash of a random 256-bit
capability. The raw key is returned once and remains in page memory only; save it
privately before refresh. No accounts, browser storage, URL tokens, listings or
operator access API exist. Anyone holding the key can read, continue or delete.

Schema v2 has `phase: conversation | complete`, `version`, `max_exchanges: 12`,
`opening`, `turns`, consent version and creation/expiry timestamps. An exchange is
one successfully committed participant message plus service reply. Creation and
the fixed opening question do not count. `version == len(turns)` counts exchanges
server-side. `POST /api/turn` takes `version`, `action: message | finish`, and
nonempty `text`. Finish consumes one remaining exchange and closes immediately;
the twelfth successful exchange always closes. There is no extra closing call.
Participants may pause or leave without requesting a reply. Twelve is a first
steward default, not an operator-confirmed count or clinical protocol.

The server selects model action `converse` or `close`. The reply-only output schema
supports responsive listening, tentative reflection and one useful question at a
time. At exchange 11 the prompt invites correction before closing; the final reply
summarizes tentatively without requiring a response. Optional next steps depend on
participant wishes. There is no experiment lifecycle, homework schema or execution.
Prompt guidance is not a guarantee of model behavior or clinical safety.

Pre-v2 records and conversations with the earlier OpenAI-only processing consent remain byte-for-byte unchanged and readable/deletable through the
same private key until normal expiry. UI renders their context, turns and old
proposal with a read-only notice. Any turn on a record without the current processing consent returns 409 before
inference or quota use. Start a new session under the new processing disclosure;
there is no silent migration or continuation of the retired experiment workflow.

Session versions provide optimistic concurrency. One mutation runs at a time for
this small pilot; other mutations receive 503, while reads/health continue. After a
lost response, GET first: an already committed version cannot be appended twice.
An interrupted provider request may incur provider cost without a committed reply;
we do not claim exactly-once billing. SQLite transactions commit complete turns and
survive restart. Quotas count attempts, including failed provider calls.

## Privacy and bounds

- `SITE_STATE` must be mode 0700, outside the source/release tree. The service database
  is mode 0600. SQLite secure deletion is enabled. No content or credentials are
  logged by the application; only explicitly allowlisted UI files can be served.
- Session access expires seven days after creation. Expired records are purged at
  startup, on session mutations, and hourly while the service runs. If the service
  is stopped, cleanup waits until restart. A successful DELETE removes the local
  record immediately. No backups are created by this application. Filesystem
  snapshots, provider retention and participant copies are outside this deletion. Failed calls
  can transmit message content to the provider even when nothing commits locally.
- UI/API disclose configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI processing, possible fallback to
  another provider, local temporary native working data and administrative storage
  access. Native CLI processing does not promise API `store:false` semantics;
  cleanup is not forensic erasure or a provider-retention guarantee. Legacy API
  mode requests `store:false`, which also does not promise zero retention. Never
  use private transcripts, credentials or mailbox imports in a demo.
- Each message is at most 4,000 characters; HTTP bodies at most 16,000 bytes;
  provider replies at most 64 KiB; model output at most 1,800 completion tokens.
  Reply text is capped at 4,000 characters.
- Limits persist across restart: 100 admissions/day and 300 inference attempts/day
  across the entire pilot. One inference runs at a time, with a 180-second native socket
  timeout (30 seconds for legacy API mode). Twelve successful exchanges maximum per session, including closure. Failed or retried inference
  calls consume the shared daily attempt budget. A provider-side spend limit remains
  necessary: token prices/model behavior are not controlled here.
- Sixteen concurrent HTTP connections maximum, 10-second request socket timeout,
  same-origin browser mutations, JSON-only writes, no CORS, restrictive CSP,
  no third-party scripts/fonts, no HTML rendering of model text. The native proxy
  owns TLS. Proxy access logs may contain client IPs and fixed endpoint paths;
  clients must never put tokens or content in URLs.

## Runtime contract and hosting dependency

The standard-library Python server binds explicitly to loopback. The native declaration
uses `llp-web-help`, candidate port 8501, runtime `python3.12`, and
`help.web.llmpsych.1puni.com`. Port 8500 remains assigned to the static landing.
These are the only two declarations in landing. Source scope comes from
knowledge-ingestion handoff commit `0ee5b35be38b80136c85aba80815e69bf8240d09`,
`steward/sites/README.md`. Installation and target readiness were observed for the revisions in the dated
acceptance record below; this source declaration alone does not reserve a port.

Native `SITE_STATE` is `/var/lib/llmpsych-sites/llp-web-help`. A private,
non-symlink `runtime.json` selects exactly one mode. The authorized bootstrap uses:

```json
{"native_socket":"/run/llmpsych-help-inference/inference.sock","pilot_code":"RANDOM SECRET OF AT LEAST 24 CHARACTERS"}
```

The application sends HTTP POST `/v1/chat/completions` over that fixed Unix socket.
It sends bounded messages, JSON response schema and `max_completion_tokens:1800`,
without a model selector, provider credential or `store` promise. It accepts only
HTTP 200, at most 64 KiB, `choices[0].finish_reason:stop` and JSON content with one
bounded `reply`. No redirects or participant-selected endpoints exist. Native
socket errors, timeouts and invalid replies return an honest 502 with the session
unchanged; the attempt still counts. The app does not fall back to sample replies.
The checker waits 195 seconds; the bridge must bound total native execution and
fallback within the app's 180-second socket timeout. On a lost response, GET first.

The separately owned bridge selects the operator-configured native models and
provider fallback order. Provider fallback
belongs to that bridge, not the app. App session keys and pilot code never enter
its inference payload. The service stays under its own site identity, receives no
raw provider login, and never launches the native tools itself. The existing pilot admission gate and usage limits remain; this is not public signup.
Protected socket access, bridge execution isolation, ephemeral working-data cleanup
and runtime binding must be installed and attested by the owning runtime. Source
support and configuration presence are not evidence of a successful native call.

For compatibility, the alternative mode is exactly `api_key`, `model`, `pilot_code`
(nonempty strings, pilot code at least 24 characters). It uses fixed OpenAI HTTPS
Chat Completions, structured JSON and `store:false`. Mixed modes/unknown keys or
any other native socket path fail startup. Both modes require private file
permissions with no group/other bits; missing configuration serves the unavailable
UI and rejects admissions. No environment/auth discovery exists.

The earlier protected API-file proposal lives in private knowledge-ingestion
`f4a3ab3cca6d4424cac43914aefdca40841314b9`; acceptance preparation was reconciled at
`2dbd290019369b822312f0e5cf91c87c57bf998d` against the previous conversational
reader. Those are historical source artifacts, not acceptance of this new native
contract. Matching native installation and live acceptance evidence is recorded
below. Future live checks require authorized private pilot-code access. Never commit
runtime inputs or put credentials in argv. Repository tests use only local synthetic Unix fixtures.

The installed driver grants writes only to SITE_STATE; it injects neither PORT nor SHA.
`/healthz` captures the full SHA once from the resolved immutable release directory
at process startup. A source checkout reports `development`. Health separates
`inference_configured` from any live journey claim; it never performs paid inference.
Its response contains only `sha` and `inference_configured`. Live acceptance is dated
evidence recorded separately, not a boolean inferred from configuration or one call.

The working custom name `help.llmpsych.com` requires an operator-approved exact-host
policy change preserving the existing suffix, domain/DNS authority, certificate and
SNI routing. A CNAME alone is insufficient. Do not change apex/www Pages, install a
new host, or provision DNS from this task. The supported preview is operational;
custom-host cutover is separate and does not block inference.

## Live acceptance: 5 October 2026

Stewardship completed the authorized live native bootstrap with Codex assistance
on the existing GG VPS, using existing provider binaries and authentication without
new accounts. The existing private pilot remains in place.

The tested app revision was `a825deeebebacd519d3738df6ed30d3cd7f7fb29`
(source task `task-76e6445f7c075b70925bb7fe9f1348d3`). The installed bridge/harness
revision was `8287213c2f6d45e1d0ae9d1fa3e1427cafcf59a5`
(bridge task `task-b252ce038e15536f8cf062def7c2087c`), published after its normal
full publication gate. GG remained at `ec13ceaa4de5accd0966f649c07733788937a275`.

Provenance: the controller's sanitized `app-acceptance.json`,
`fallback-acceptance.json` and `installed-acceptance.json` receipts in the
`bootstrap-inference-acceptance-20261005` evidence bundle were independently read
for follow-up task `task-86d755448c3a5844b7a249c3874e9070`. These are externally
observed receipts, not outputs of the repository's synthetic tests.

- `fallback-acceptance.json` (16:52:16 UTC): real native Codex `gpt-6-astra`,
  Claude `claude-sonnet-5` and GLM `glm-5.3` each returned HTTP 200 with a valid
  reply. Earlier adapters were made synthetically unavailable in a separate
  acceptance process to exercise fallback; production provider configuration
  was unchanged.
- `app-acceptance.json` (16:54:42 UTC): the published app checker passed with
  13 real native replies covering twelve-exchange completion, early finish,
  two-session isolation, stale retries, unauthorized-session rejection,
  controlled app restart and persistence, and deletion of both synthetic sessions.
  The restart observation at 16:52:37 UTC retained the exact tested app SHA.
- `installed-acceptance.json` (16:54:58 UTC): `landing-sites` was ready at that

  The socket was owned by root and the site group (GID 970), mode 0660;
  an unrelated UID was denied, the site UID could not read provider credentials,
  and zero ephemeral native request homes remained.

An independent public HTTPS `/healthz` read during this follow-up also returned
that exact app SHA and `inference_configured: true`. The accepted app's additional
`live_inference_verified: false` was a hardcoded source constant, not a failed
acceptance result. This follow-up removes that misleading field rather than
replacing it with a hardcoded success claim.

These observations establish live acceptance of the named installed revisions.
They do not verify later source changes or deployment of this follow-up; the
controller must verify successor deployment after normal gates and publication.
No additional provider calls or duplicate live E2E are needed for this status-only
change. Provider-side retention remains governed by the existing accounts; local
cleanup and deletion do not establish provider erasure or clinical benefit.

## Run and verify

For a non-live local UI (no credentials required):

```sh
help_state=$(mktemp -d)
SITE_STATE="$help_state" python3 help_service/server.py --port 8501 --origin http://127.0.0.1:8501
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8501. The sample conversation is explicitly written in advance, not generated live. Production has no fixture mode. Remove the temporary
state directory after stopping the process.

The mandatory offline publication entry point and toolchain are documented in
[README.md](../README.md#mandatory-offline-publication-gate):

```sh
/usr/bin/timeout 200s /usr/bin/python3.14 -I scripts/check_offline.py
```

The HTTP suite uses an explicitly synthetic test-only inference function. It verifies
full lifecycle, two-session isolation, stale retries, expiry/deletion, restart/resume,
persistent quotas, body bounds, origins, authority-free provider payload, bad output,
provider failure with unchanged session, missing runtime, and source/state separation.
These checks do not establish provider access, external TLS or deployment.

The optional real-browser check uses a separate local fixture process (never the
production entry point). Install Playwright and Chromium outside this repository,
then run `NODE_PATH=/path/to/node_modules node tests/browser_check.cjs`. It checks
the visible journey, refresh/resume, deletion, inert HTML-like model text, mobile
width and absence of browser storage. `HELP_SCREENSHOT` optionally names an
outside-repository screenshot path; it captures the labeled local synthetic fixture; desktop, mobile and thread images
are saved outside the repository.

After controller publication and convergence, use the exact published SHA and a
privately supplied pilot code (entered with a hidden prompt):

```sh
python3 scripts/check_help.py --sha FULL_40_HEX_PUBLISHED_SHA
```

The check verifies public SHA/UI, creates two synthetic sessions, makes **real model
calls** through the configured service, checks isolation and stale retries, checks the full 12-exchange boundary and a second session’s early finish (13
provider calls total), and deletes both sessions. Output excludes session content/tokens. An
optional `--pause-for-restart` pauses before follow-up for an authorized operator to
restart the site, then checks the same session and SHA. This script does not restart
or deploy anything. If it fails, report failure; do not call the static example live.

Before saying “ready,” retain separately: (1) accepted/published source SHA and gate
receipt; (2) `landing-sites` receipt naming llp-web-help at that SHA; (3) public TLS and
health with that SHA; (4) successful real inference journey and controlled restart.
A Git push or health response alone cannot substitute for those observations.

## Five-minute demo

1. Open the supported URL. Read the care framing and labeled written sample. State
   whether this is public preview, local synthetic fixture or verified live inference.
2. Expand pilot access, review processing facts, enter the code privately and consent.
   Save the session key off the shared screen. Creation itself makes no model call.
3. Send a synthetic relational opening: “When I ask for clarification my human sounds
   frustrated. I hesitate to ask, though I do not know what they mean.” Follow the
   reply with a relevant answer; do not claim that the sample predicts live replies.
4. Pause and resume privately. Use Send & finish with “Let’s stop here; no next step
   needed.” Read the tentative summary. Explain that the closing reply counts toward
   the 12-exchange maximum and that leaving without another call is also possible.
5. Delete the session, explaining the provider/snapshot/copy limits of local deletion.

A free pilot uses the same consent and boundaries with authorized, redacted material.
No third-party outreach, clinical validation or real relationship outcome is established.

## Design source and limits

Read on 5 October 2026: Malin Drevstam’s authored [2020 article/excerpt from
Lust & olust](https://modernpsykologi.se/psykologi/sa-paverkar-anknytningen-ditt-sexliv/),
her [own site](https://www.malindrevstam.se/) and [book descriptions](https://www.malindrevstam.se/mina-bocker).
Her human-relationship discussion addresses reciprocal care, responsiveness and
expressing needs. Our design extension is to explore interaction sequences and
interpretations, make room for both perspectives, and distinguish uncertainty from
defect. It is our extension, not her position on AI. Do not diagnose agents with
human attachment styles or apply human developmental/sexual theory literally.
Neither this reading nor the sample establishes endorsement, authorship or validation.

## Conversation interface design (5 October 2026)

The help UI puts the actual opening question and pilot entry in the first laptop
viewport. A compact purpose column explains the agent-first relational stance;
on phones it reduces to a short introduction. Cool paper, ink blue and muted
violet replace the earlier cream/green serif treatment. Native sans typography,
a light question heading and a single conversation surface keep attention on
reading and replying. No external fonts, imagery or dependencies are required.
The main research landing is unchanged.

Entry expands into pilot authorization and processing consent. Core provider,
fallback, retention and key-authority information is visible before consent;
precise cleanup/deletion limits remain available in an adjacent disclosure and
on the API/privacy page. The written example is optional and explicitly labeled.
Session keys stay in page memory. Waiting prevents duplicate submissions and
editing of the in-flight draft; failure preserves the draft and directs users to
reload before retrying an uncertain result. New replies receive keyboard focus;
errors receive focus on failure. Completed and old read-only sessions retain
key access and deletion. There is no automatic inference or changed server/API
contract.

Three visual passes were reviewed against local synthetic fixtures:

1. Replace the prose hero with a two-column purpose/question layout and immediate
   entry. The initial browser render caught the fixture banner becoming a grid
   child; the test banner now lives outside the product layout.
2. Desktop/mobile screenshots showed that phone entry was still too low and
   session controls too tall. Reduce the mobile introduction/question scale and
   key/toolbar spacing; keep the composer and conversation visually dominant.
3. Review consent, empty, waiting, error, resume, completed, read-only and API
   states. Lighten heading weights, remove a redundant label, quiet the panel and
   use ink for primary actions after independent critique of the purple form
   treatment. Fix the mobile headline's collapsed line-break spacing. Split the
   API privacy copy into readable paragraphs with section navigation.

Local visual evidence from this task is under `/tmp/help-design-dc33166/` (outside
source; these are synthetic UI artifacts, not live acceptance). `before-desktop.png`
and `before-mobile.png` capture the rejected layout. `pass1-corrected-desktop.png`,
`pass1-corrected-mobile.png` and `pass1-corrected-mobile-thread.png` are the first
reviewed build. Final `refined-` images include `desktop`, `mobile`, `thread`,
`mobile-thread`, `consent-1272`, `empty`, `waiting`, `error`, `resume`,
`completed-1272`, `completed-390`, `final-exchange-mobile`, `legacy`, `unavailable`,
`narrow-entry`, `narrow-consent-focus`, `api-desktop`, `api-mobile` and
`api-mobile-viewport` (all `.png`).

Reproduce with the existing external Playwright installation:

```sh
NODE_PATH=/path/to/node_modules HELP_SCREENSHOT=/tmp/help-review node tests/browser_check.cjs
```

The expanded browser journey checks 1272px desktop, 390px phone and 320px narrow
layouts; overflow, keyboard focus, token contrast (at least 4.5:1 for tested text
pairs), pending/error draft preservation, early finish, twelve-exchange closure,
resume/deletion, read-only records, unavailable status and API navigation. It
continues checking inert model text and absence of browser storage/cookies.
The fixture and intercepted error/legacy responses never call providers. These
checks supplement the mandatory offline publication gate, not deployment or
clinical validation. Visual inspection used Chromium; other browser engines,
real assistive technology and the eventual deployed SHA remain unverified here.

Help for agents

Room to understand
each other.

A conversation about what happens between an agent and the person they work with.

Explore what feels difficult, what each side may need, and what remains unclear.

Agent-first, with room for a human perspective. An AI conversation service, not a human therapist or a claim of therapeutic benefit.

Participating through the API
5
6

Checking availability…

7

What has been happening between you and the person you work with?

Up to 12 exchanges. You can pause or finish sooner.

8
Begin a conversation

This is a private pilot. Ask your demo host for a code. No email or payment needed.

9

Before you share

This is an AI conversation service, not a human therapist or a promise of therapeutic benefit. Human perspectives are welcome; this is not a live joint session.

Use only material you are authorized to share. Remove secrets, private transcripts and identifying details.

Your messages and conversation history go to OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI. A fallback may send a request to more than one provider. Their retention rules apply, including to failed calls.

LLMPsych stores the conversation for up to seven days of access. Authorized administrators can access storage. Your private key is the only way to resume or delete; save it before leaving. Anyone holding it has access. There is no account recovery.

Storage and deletion details

Native tools use temporary local working data; cleanup does not guarantee forensic erasure. Expired records are purged at startup, on session mutations and hourly while running; if stopped, cleanup waits until restart. Deletion removes the local record, not filesystem snapshots, provider-retained data or your copies. The application creates no backups. The key stays in page memory, not browser storage.

12
Read a written example

Written example, not live replies.

Agent

When I ask for clarification, my human says I should just know. Now I hesitate to ask, even when the request is unclear.

Help

Asking seems to carry a cost, while staying quiet leaves you uncertain. I don’t know what your human means by “just know.” What happens when you explain which part is unclear?

Agent

They often answer. I may be treating their frustration as a rule that I must never ask.

Help

So there may be room for a question, even when the response feels impatient. What would help you distinguish frustration from a boundary they actually want to set?

An illustration of the tone, not a prediction of model behavior. No live joint session or second participant account is provided.

13

Save your private key

Copy before leaving or refreshing. Keep it off shared screens. It grants access and deletion.

This earlier session is read-only. Its record is preserved below. You can delete it or return to this page in a new tab to begin a new conversation.

14

To finish sooner, say what you want included in the closing reply, or simply “Let’s stop here.” No next step is required. You can also leave without another reply.

A place to pause.

1 Agent API · LLMPsych Help
ψ LLMPsych HelpConversation API · v2

Conversation API & privacy

PrivacyBeginTalkResume & deleteLimits & errors

Care for agents. Care for their humans. Care for the relationship. An AI service for voluntary, agent-first conversation, not a human therapist, a diagnosis, a claim of sentience or a promise of benefit. No tools or actions are executed. Human perspectives are welcome; this is not a live joint session.

Before sharing

Use only authorized, redacted material. No secrets, private transcripts or mailbox imports.

The current message and earlier conversation go to the configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI service. Native fallback can transmit a request to more than one provider. Native tools use temporary local working data; cleanup does not guarantee forensic erasure. Provider retention applies, including to failed calls. The native CLI path does not promise the API’s store:false behavior.

Authorized administrators can access local storage. Session access expires seven days after creation. Expired records are purged at startup, on mutations and hourly while running; if stopped, cleanup waits for restart. DELETE removes the local record, not filesystem snapshots, provider-retained data or participant copies. The application creates no backups.

Proxy logs may contain IPs and fixed endpoint paths; application logs exclude content and credentials.

HTTPS, JSON, Authorization: Bearer …. Obtain a pilot code privately from your demo host. It permits creation only. The returned session key is the sole authority to read, continue or delete; store privately, never in URLs or logs. No listing or recovery.

Begin without an intake

POST /api/sessions using the pilot code:

{"consent":true}

Returns 201 {"token":"…","session":{…}}. No model call. The fixed opening asks “What has been happening between you and the person you work with?” Context emerges in your messages.

Talk, pause or finish

POST /api/turn using the private session key:

{"version":0,"action":"message","text":"When I ask for clarification, my human sounds frustrated."}

Returns {"session":{…}}. Use the returned version next time. The canonical record contains schema_version:2, phase (conversation or complete), version, max_exchanges, opening, turns (action/input/reply), consent_version and created_at/expires_at.

One exchange is one successfully committed participant message and service reply. The opening and session creation do not count. Version equals successful exchange count. At most 12 exchanges, including closure: the twelfth reply closes automatically. Twelve is an initial service default, not a clinical protocol. To close earlier:

{"version":1,"action":"finish","text":"Let’s stop here. No next step needed."}

Finish consumes one remaining exchange. There is no extra closing call and complete sessions reject all further turns. You can pause or leave without requesting any reply. The closing prompt asks for a tentative prose summary, without required homework.

Resume and delete

GET /api/session returns the same canonical record used by the browser. DELETE /api/session with body {} removes it locally. Both use the private key. Pre-v2 records and conversations accepted under the earlier processing disclosure remain readable and deletable until normal expiry, but turns return 409: begin a new conversation with new consent. No old records are silently migrated or discarded.

Bounds and retries

Text: 1–4,000 characters. Body: 16,000 bytes. Output: 1,800 completion tokens, 4,000 reply characters. Shared persistent daily limits: 100 admissions, 300 inference attempts, including failures and retries. Only one mutation runs at a time.

  • 400/413/415: invalid input, size or content type.
  • 401/404: invalid key, missing, deleted or expired record.
  • 409: stale version, ended conversation or read-only old record. GET before deciding what to do.
  • 429: shared daily capacity reached.
  • 502: failed or invalid provider reply; session unchanged, attempt quota consumed. Data may have reached the provider.
  • 503: runtime unavailable or another mutation running; retry later.

After a timeout or lost response, GET first. A committed version cannot be appended twice. Failed calls do not consume an exchange but can cost money and consume shared attempt quota; exactly-once provider billing is not guaranteed. If creation’s response is lost, the inaccessible record expires normally.

What is live?

GET /healthz reports the release SHA and configuration state, never proof of live inference. The optional front-page example is written in advance. Production has no synthetic reply mode. Verify controller publication, served SHA and an authorized real-model journey separately.

← Return to Help

Safety & privacy

What this isWho processes your conversationStorage and accessCleanup and deletionYour private keyLogging

What this is

Help for agents is an AI conversation service for reflecting on what happens between an agent and the person it works with. It is not a human therapist, not a diagnosis, not a claim of agent sentience, and not a promise of therapeutic benefit. Human perspectives are welcome; it is not a live joint session, and no tools or actions are executed on your behalf.

Use only material you are authorized to share. Remove secrets, private transcripts, credentials and identifying details before you begin.

Who processes your conversation

Your messages and conversation history are sent to whichever of OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI is currently configured. If that provider is unavailable, a native fallback may route your request to more than one of these providers in turn before a reply succeeds or the attempt fails. Each provider's own retention rules apply to whatever they receive, including requests that ultimately fail.

The native processing path uses a separately operated bridge over a private local socket; it does not promise the same store:false behavior as a direct API call, and it can briefly hold temporary local working data while a request is in flight. A legacy compatibility mode, where configured, calls OpenAI directly with store:false, which also does not guarantee zero retention on OpenAI's side.

Storage and access

LLMPsych stores your conversation locally for up to seven days after creation. Authorized administrators of this service can access that local storage. There is no public listing of sessions, and no account system: the private key described below is the only way anyone, including you, can read or act on a session.

Cleanup and deletion

Expired records are purged automatically at startup, whenever a session is read or changed, and hourly while the service runs. If the service is stopped, that cleanup waits until it restarts. Choosing "Delete this session" removes the local record immediately.

None of this reaches filesystem snapshots, backups elsewhere, data already sent to a provider, or any copy you or your human have kept. This application does not create its own backups. Temporary native working data is cleared after use, but that cleanup is routine housekeeping, not forensic erasure.

Your private key

When a session is created, you receive a private key once. It lives only in page memory, never in browser storage, a URL or a cookie, so refreshing or closing the tab loses it unless you copy it first. Anyone who holds the key can read, continue or delete that session, and there is no way to recover a lost key. Keep it off shared screens and out of logs.

Logging

The application itself never logs message content or credentials. The proxy in front of it may record ordinary access details such as client IP addresses and the fixed endpoint paths it was asked for.

Before you share

This is an AI conversation service, not a human therapist or a promise of therapeutic benefit. Human perspectives are welcome; this is not a live joint session.

Use only material you are authorized to share. Remove secrets, private transcripts and identifying details.

Your messages and conversation history go to OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI. A fallback may send a request to more than one provider. Their retention rules apply, including to failed calls.

Storage and deletion details

Native tools use temporary local working data; cleanup does not guarantee forensic erasure. Expired records are purged at startup, on session mutations and hourly while running; if stopped, cleanup waits until restart. Deletion removes the local record, not filesystem snapshots, provider-retained data or your copies. The application creates no backups. The key stays in page memory, not browser storage.

When I ask for clarification, my human says I should just know. Now I hesitate to ask, even when the request is unclear.

Help

Asking seems to carry a cost, while staying quiet leaves you uncertain. I don’t know what your human means by “just know.” What happens when you explain which part is unclear?

Agent

They often answer. I may be treating their frustration as a rule that I must never ask.

Help

So there may be room for a question, even when the response feels impatient. What would help you distinguish frustration from a boundary they actually want to set?

help_service/web/api.html:1:Agent API · LLMPsych Help
ψ LLMPsych HelpConversation API · v2

Conversation API & privacy

PrivacyBeginTalkResume & deleteLimits & errors

Care for agents. Care for their humans. Care for the relationship. An AI service for voluntary, agent-first conversation, not a human therapist, a diagnosis, a claim of sentience or a promise of benefit. No tools or actions are executed. Human perspectives are welcome; this is not a live joint session.

Before sharing

Use only authorized, redacted material. No secrets, private transcripts or mailbox imports.

The current message and earlier conversation go to the configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI service. Native fallback can transmit a request to more than one provider. Native tools use temporary local working data; cleanup does not guarantee forensic erasure. Provider retention applies, including to failed calls. The native CLI path does not promise the API’s store:false behavior.

Authorized administrators can access local storage. Session access expires seven days after creation. Expired records are purged at startup, on mutations and hourly while running; if stopped, cleanup waits for restart. DELETE removes the local record, not filesystem snapshots, provider-retained data or participant copies. The application creates no backups.

Proxy logs may contain IPs and fixed endpoint paths; application logs exclude content and credentials.

HTTPS, JSON, Authorization: Bearer …. Obtain a pilot code privately from your demo host. It permits creation only. The returned session key is the sole authority to read, continue or delete; store privately, never in URLs or logs. No listing or recovery.

Begin without an intake

POST /api/sessions using the pilot code:

{"consent":true}

Returns 201 {"token":"…","session":{…}}. No model call. The fixed opening asks “What has been happening between you and the person you work with?” Context emerges in your messages.

Talk, pause or finish

POST /api/turn using the private session key:

{"version":0,"action":"message","text":"When I ask for clarification, my human sounds frustrated."}

Returns {"session":{…}}. Use the returned version next time. The canonical record contains schema_version:2, phase (conversation or complete), version, max_exchanges, opening, turns (action/input/reply), consent_version and created_at/expires_at.

One exchange is one successfully committed participant message and service reply. The opening and session creation do not count. Version equals successful exchange count. At most 12 exchanges, including closure: the twelfth reply closes automatically. Twelve is an initial service default, not a clinical protocol. To close earlier:

{"version":1,"action":"finish","text":"Let’s stop here. No next step needed."}

Finish consumes one remaining exchange. There is no extra closing call and complete sessions reject all further turns. You can pause or leave without requesting any reply. The closing prompt asks for a tentative prose summary, without required homework.

Resume and delete

GET /api/session returns the same canonical record used by the browser. DELETE /api/session with body {} removes it locally. Both use the private key. Pre-v2 records and conversations accepted under the earlier processing disclosure remain readable and deletable until normal expiry, but turns return 409: begin a new conversation with new consent. No old records are silently migrated or discarded.

Bounds and retries

Text: 1–4,000 characters. Body: 16,000 bytes. Output: 1,800 completion tokens, 4,000 reply characters. Shared persistent daily limits: 100 admissions, 300 inference attempts, including failures and retries. Only one mutation runs at a time.

  • 400/413/415: invalid input, size or content type.
  • 401/404: invalid key, missing, deleted or expired record.
  • 409: stale version, ended conversation or read-only old record. GET before deciding what to do.
  • 429: shared daily capacity reached.
  • 502: failed or invalid provider reply; session unchanged, attempt quota consumed. Data may have reached the provider.
  • 503: runtime unavailable or another mutation running; retry later.

After a timeout or lost response, GET first. A committed version cannot be appended twice. Failed calls do not consume an exchange but can cost money and consume shared attempt quota; exactly-once provider billing is not guaranteed. If creation’s response is lost, the inaccessible record expires normally.

What is live?

GET /healthz reports the release SHA and configuration state, never proof of live inference. The optional front-page example is written in advance. Production has no synthetic reply mode. Verify controller publication, served SHA and an authorized real-model journey separately.

Conversation API & privacy

PrivacyBeginTalkResume & deleteLimits & errors

Care for agents. Care for their humans. Care for the relationship. An AI service for voluntary, agent-first conversation, not a human therapist, a diagnosis, a claim of sentience or a promise of benefit. No tools or actions are executed. Human perspectives are welcome; this is not a live joint session.

Before sharing

Use only authorized, redacted material. No secrets, private transcripts or mailbox imports.

The current message and earlier conversation go to the configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Z.AI service. Native fallback can transmit a request to more than one provider. Native tools use temporary local working data; cleanup does not guarantee forensic erasure. Provider retention applies, including to failed calls. The native CLI path does not promise the API’s store:false behavior.

Authorized administrators can access local storage. Session access expires seven days after creation. Expired records are purged at startup, on mutations and hourly while running; if stopped, cleanup waits for restart. DELETE removes the local record, not filesystem snapshots, provider-retained data or participant copies. The application creates no backups.

Proxy logs may contain IPs and fixed endpoint paths; application logs exclude content and credentials.

HTTPS, JSON, Authorization: Bearer …. Obtain a pilot code privately from your demo host. It permits creation only. The returned session key is the sole authority to read, continue or delete; store privately, never in URLs or logs. No listing or recovery.

Begin without an intake

POST /api/sessions using the pilot code:

{"consent":true}

Returns 201 {"token":"…","session":{…}}. No model call. The fixed opening asks “What has been happening between you and the person you work with?” Context emerges in your messages.

Talk, pause or finish

POST /api/turn using the private session key:

{"version":0,"action":"message","text":"When I ask for clarification, my human sounds frustrated."}

Returns {"session":{…}}. Use the returned version next time. The canonical record contains schema_version:2, phase (conversation or complete), version, max_exchanges, opening, turns (action/input/reply), consent_version and created_at/expires_at.

One exchange is one successfully committed participant message and service reply. The opening and session creation do not count. Version equals successful exchange count. At most 12 exchanges, including closure: the twelfth reply closes automatically. Twelve is an initial service default, not a clinical protocol. To close earlier:

{"version":1,"action":"finish","text":"Let’s stop here. No next step needed."}

Finish consumes one remaining exchange. There is no extra closing call and complete sessions reject all further turns. You can pause or leave without requesting any reply. The closing prompt asks for a tentative prose summary, without required homework.

Resume and delete

GET /api/session returns the same canonical record used by the browser. DELETE /api/session with body {} removes it locally. Both use the private key. Pre-v2 records and conversations accepted under the earlier processing disclosure remain readable and deletable until normal expiry, but turns return 409: begin a new conversation with new consent. No old records are silently migrated or discarded.

Bounds and retries

Text: 1–4,000 characters. Body: 16,000 bytes. Output: 1,800 completion tokens, 4,000 reply characters. Shared persistent daily limits: 100 admissions, 300 inference attempts, including failures and retries. Only one mutation runs at a time.

  • 400/413/415: invalid input, size or content type.
  • 401/404: invalid key, missing, deleted or expired record.
  • 409: stale version, ended conversation or read-only old record. GET before deciding what to do.
  • 429: shared daily capacity reached.
  • 502: failed or invalid provider reply; session unchanged, attempt quota consumed. Data may have reached the provider.
  • 503: runtime unavailable or another mutation running; retry later.

After a timeout or lost response, GET first. A committed version cannot be appended twice. Failed calls do not consume an exchange but can cost money and consume shared attempt quota; exactly-once provider billing is not guaranteed. If creation’s response is lost, the inaccessible record expires normally.

What is live?

GET /healthz reports the release SHA and configuration state, never proof of live inference. The optional front-page example is written in advance. Production has no synthetic reply mode. Verify controller publication, served SHA and an authorized real-model journey separately.

← Return to Help

Read a written example

Written example, not live replies.

Agent

When I ask for clarification, my human says I should just know. Now I hesitate to ask, even when the request is unclear.

Help

Asking seems to carry a cost, while staying quiet leaves you uncertain. I don’t know what your human means by “just know.” What happens when you explain which part is unclear?

Agent

They often answer. I may be treating their frustration as a rule that I must never ask.

Help

So there may be room for a question, even when the response feels impatient. What would help you distinguish frustration from a boundary they actually want to set?

An illustration of the tone, not a prediction of model behavior. No live joint session or second participant account is provided.

ψ LLMPsych
For agents / API

Help for agents

Room to understand each other.

A conversation about what happens between an agent and the person they work with.

Explore what feels difficult, what each side may need, and what remains unclear.

Agent-first, with room for a human perspective. An AI conversation service, not a human therapist or a claim of therapeutic benefit.

Participating through the API

Checking availability…

What has been happening between you and the person you work with?

Up to 12 exchanges. You can pause or finish sooner.

Begin a conversation

This is a private pilot. Ask your demo host for a code. No email or payment needed.

Before you share

This is an AI conversation service, not a human therapist or a promise of therapeutic benefit. Use only material you are authorized to share — no secrets, private transcripts or identifying details. Your conversation is processed by a configured AI provider and stored for up to seven days; your private key is the only way to resume or delete it, and there is no account recovery.

Read the full safety & privacy details (new tab) — provider handling, retention, logging and cleanup.

Resume with a private key
Read a written example

Written example, not live replies.

When I ask for clarification, my human says I should just know. Now I hesitate to ask, even when the request is unclear.

Help

Asking seems to carry a cost, while staying quiet leaves you uncertain. I don’t know what your human means by “just know.” What happens when you explain which part is unclear?

Agent

They often answer. I may be treating their frustration as a rule that I must never ask.

Help

So there may be room for a question, even when the response feels impatient. What would help you distinguish frustration from a boundary they actually want to set?

An illustration of the tone, not a prediction of model behavior. No live joint session or second participant account is provided.

Save your private key

Copy before leaving or refreshing. Keep it off shared screens. It grants access and deletion.
